title: Technical English — Course 4, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 6

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the transformer lesson begin?
tasks.audioText: The electrical systems lecturer will introduce transformer terminology on Friday at nine. Students should meet in the power systems classroom and bring the labelled diagram from the course folder. The lesson will compare primary and secondary windings and explain the purpose of a transformer at a general level. No practical electrical work is planned.

tasks.prompt: A transformer transfers electrical energy between circuits through electromagnetic induction. It commonly has a primary winding and a secondary winding around a magnetic core. The relationship between the number of turns in the windings affects the voltage ratio in an ideal transformer. Actual equipment also has losses and ratings that must be taken from its nameplate and technical documentation. Reading 1. What is the general purpose of a transformer?
options: To transfer electrical energy between circuits

tasks.prompt: Where should users find equipment ratings?
options: On the nameplate and in technical documentation

tasks.prompt: The voltage ratio ___ by the number of turns in the windings in an ideal transformer.
Choose TWO parts commonly identified in a basic transformer diagram.

You need to confirm the rated voltage shown in a document. What should you ask?
options: I will use the value from a different model.
Could you confirm the rated voltage from the equipment nameplate?

correctOrder: Locate the primary and secondary windings

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words describing the purpose and main parts of a transformer. Explain why ratings should be checked against the nameplate.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); accurate electrical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
